validated_results.title: Oxidant-antioxidant levels in patients with bladder tumours.
validated_results.journal: The aging male : the official journal of the International Society for the Study of the Aging Male
validated_results.reason: Original case-control comparison of serum antioxidant biomarker levels (reduced glutathione, GST, SOD, glutathione reductase) between bladder tumour patients and healthy controls, framed as etiopathogenesis of bladder tumour.

extraction.comparison_type: Bladder tumour patients versus healthy volunteer controls (serum antioxidant enzyme/glutathione levels)
extraction.population: Patients with superficial bladder tumour and healthy volunteers

sample_size.excerpt: Thirty patients with bladder tumour with superficial bladder tumour and 27 normal healthy volunteers were included in the study. Four cc of venous blood was taken from these patients and volunteers in the control group and centrifuged at 5000 rpm for 10 minutes and divided into serum and plasma.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 27 + 30 = 57

cases.excerpt: Thirty patients with bladder tumour with superficial bladder tumour and 27 normal healthy volunteers were included in the study.

comparison.excerpt: Antioxidant parameters (glutathione-s-transferase, reduced glutathione, superoxide dismutase and glutathione reductase) in the serum of patients with bladder tumours were found statistically significantly lower than control group

exposure_measurement.excerpt: The activities of xanthine oxidase, glutathione reductase, glutathione-s transferase, reduced glutathione and superoxide dismutase enzymes in serum were then measured spectrophotometrically.

extraction.ethnicity_basis: NA: no field-specific ethnicity evidence was available

parallel_r3_gate_reasons: JBI remains Fair after Claude R2
important quantitative evidence remains missing or invalid: ci_lower, ci_upper, effect_size, effect_type, p_value

validated_results.title: Copper and zinc levels in plasma and cancerous tissues and their relation with expression of VEGF and HIF-1 in the pathogenesis of muscle invasive urothelial bladder cancer: a case-controlled clinical study.
validated_results.journal: Environmental science and pollution research international
validated_results.reason: Case-controlled clinical study reporting plasma copper levels in bladder cancer patients versus matched controls with logistic regression identifying plasma Cu as a risk factor for bladder cancer development.

extraction.comparison_type: Bladder cancer patients versus matched controls (plasma Cu levels; logistic regression)
extraction.population: Transitional bladder cell carcinoma patients and matched controls

sample_size.excerpt: Plasma levels of Cu and Zn were determined in 66 transitional bladder cell carcinoma patients (BC group) and 60 matched controls.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 66 + 60 = 126

cases.excerpt: To evaluate Cu and Zn levels in bladder cancer (BC) patients and their relationship with expression of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and hypoxia-inducible factor 1 (HIF-1). Plasma levels of Cu and Zn were determined in 66 transitional bladder cell carcinoma patients (BC group) and 60 matched controls.

comparison.excerpt: Logistic regression analysis revealed that the increase in plasma Cu/Zn ratio and plasma Cu and the decrease in plasma Zn may be risk factors for development of bladder cancer.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Plasma levels of Cu and Zn were determined in 66 transitional bladder cell carcinoma patients (BC group) and 60 matched controls.
